items.title: Steve Buckingham, interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 25, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I’m flying you tonight to Los Angeles to meet with Melissa Manchester to do her next album... Our first album was successful, and her second album. And we did a Christmas album in the late 90s. I mean we’re still friends.

ctx.x: That’s my question, like what’s the first interaction like?

A meeting. After I did “I Love the Night Life” the next person to call me was Clive Davis and flew me to New York and he quizzed me. He played me demos of songs. He’d play me records that they were getting ready to release. And he would be very specific. “Do you think this is a hit? Why or why not?” He was very specific and we were there hours the first time I met with Clive in New York. And we left after that first day and he said, “Put together some songs” he’s a song man to this day, he’s what 86 or so now,…

successful, and her second album. And we did a Christmas album in the late 90s. I mean we’re still friends. I just went to see her play a few months ago, a couple of months ago. We’re still great friends. But that’s usually how — you have to meet with them ahead of time to see if there’s a chemistry.
